close_reason: Replaced assert!(a == b, msg) with assert_eq!(a, b, msg) in LintRunner::new's debug-only duplicate-id check, for richer assertion diagnostic output.
description:
Pass 2 idiom finding under epic PKIX-qwzx.

`pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:636-639` uses `assert!` with an equality predicate where
`assert_eq!` is idiomatic and gives better error messages:

```rust
assert!(
    ids.len() == original_len,
    \"duplicate lint IDs will produce confusing deviation behavior\"
);
```

Idiomatic:
```rust
assert_eq!(
    ids.len(), original_len,
    \"duplicate lint IDs will produce confusing deviation behavior\"
);
```

Difference at runtime: `assert_eq!` prints both sides of the comparison
(`assertion `left == right` failed: ...; left: 3; right: 4`), which is
significantly more useful than \"assertion failed: ids.len() == original_len\".

This is wrapped in `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` so it only fires in dev builds,
but the diagnostic improvement is the whole point.

Caught by clippy's `unnecessary_cast` ↔ wait, no — actually by
`clippy::manual_assert` and `clippy::eq_op` neighborhood; specifically
`clippy::assertions_on_constants` does not catch this either. The lint that
catches it is `clippy::nonminimal_bool` only sometimes; in practice this is a
manual-spot finding, not a lint hit.

Fix: change `assert!(a == b, msg)` to `assert_eq!(a, b, msg)`.
title: (IDIOM) P4: assert!(a == b, ...) instead of assert_eq!(a, b, ...) in LintRunner::new debug check
